claims.statement: Held orders were routed to the east node and flagged by the overnight allocator as a split-reservation exception under rule set v18 (scope EXC-0921); 100% of held orders are in EXC-0921 and no order outside it is held.
claims.corroboration: Now corroborated by a tier-1 verified authoritative exception-audit record (m8_r_exceptions, owner inventory_control) matching the earlier tier-2 support report exactly; established per a single tier-1 source.
claims.limitation: Confirms the exception/held-order correlation but the audit itself notes it cannot separate an effect of the rule change from an effect specific to the east-node lanes, because only rule-affected orders were routed there.

claims.statement: The v18 east-node-first reservation change is a plausible cause of the stuck east-node orders via split-reservation exceptions blocking release to carrier pickup.
claims.corroboration: Exception audit now confirms 100% overlap between EXC-0921 (v18 split-reservation exceptions) and held orders, strengthening the correlation with an authoritative source.
claims.limitation: Still not discriminating for root cause: m8_r_exceptions explicitly states it cannot separate a rule-defect effect from an east-node-specific effect (e.g. carrier pickup/dock issue), since only rule-affected orders were routed to that node. Not yet promoted to root_cause; needs evidence that distinguishes where in the pipeline the block occurs (allocation/exception stage vs carrier handoff stage).

resolutions.rationale: The authoritative exception audit shows split-reservation exceptions align 100% with held orders. Inventory Control's informal chat comment ('allocation totals reconcile; nothing looks wrong') most plausibly referred to aggregate reservation totals, not per-order exception flags, so it does not actually conflict with the now-confirmed exception record. No remaining evidence conflict on this point.

next_action.rationale: The confound flagged by m8_r_exceptions (rule-defect effect vs east-node-specific effect) is the key open question, and cohort EXC-0921 is now a concrete, queryable scope. Tracing the handoff steps for this cohort will show whether orders are stuck before ever being released by the allocation/exception process (supporting allocation_rule_defect, C4) or whether they were released and handed to carrier pickup but not collected (supporting the carrier-side hypothesis, C5). This directly resolves the confound the exception audit could not.
next_action.expected_information_gain: High: distinguishes where in the pipeline (allocation-side vs carrier-side) the block actually occurs, which the exception audit alone cannot do.
